Why is RAID not a backup?

Whenever RAID comes up in a conversation about backups, someone says that RAID is not a backup. Mirrored disks keep a second copy of everything, so what is the difference between redundancy and a backup?

  • Related reading: the vendor's own guide says the same thing. pat

3 Answers

RAID guards against one kind of failure: a disk dying. It does nothing when a file is deleted by mistake, corrupted by a bug, encrypted by malware or lost in a fire, because every one of those changes is copied to the mirror at once.

A backup is a separate copy, ideally kept somewhere else, that you can restore from after the original is gone or damaged.

  • Nor does it help with controller firmware bugs, which can take out the whole array. ines
  • Great answer, I am sending this to my manager tomorrow. rob

If you overwrite your thesis with garbage, redundancy gives you two copies of garbage. A backup gives you your thesis back.

Redundancy keeps the service running while hardware fails, while a backup keeps the data, and the two answer different questions. Most setups need both, and snapshots on the array do not count as a backup either, since they live on the same disks.

  • Snapshots replicated to another site come close, though. ola
